title: Accessing memory by address
summary: Locate a memory cell by adding its row base address and column offset, then read the data stored there.
description: On the left is a vertical memory module whose black chip area connects via two gray lines to the memory grid on the right. Those physical chips are not at the same level of representation as the dark cells indicating used memory inside the grid.

The grid shows 5 rows and 8 columns: row base addresses are 0x0000, 0x0010, 0x0020, 0x0030, and 0x0040, and column offsets run from 00 to 07; ellipses on the right and bottom indicate additional cells not drawn. Light cells represent free memory and dark cells represent used memory; free memory does not mean the cell contains the number 0.

frames.title: Accessing memory by address
frames.explanation: Adding the row base address and column offset pinpoints a cell. For example, 0x0020 plus offset 04 gives 0x0024, yielding data value 2. The two read callouts below the grid correspond to the two rows in the table. An address identifies a location, whereas data is the content stored at that location; the grid is an addressing diagram rather than the physical circuit layout of a memory chip.
